title: token-velocity-vs-p90-cost-snapshot-walkthrough
content:
Purpose and framing:
This is a lightweight, shareable walkthrough of an internal micro-benchmark series exploring how token velocity (tokens produced/consumed per second per session cohort) interacts with P90 response latency and per-1k-token cost. Goal is to produce an operational snapshot that product/solutions teams can use to pick latency targets for pricing tiers and recommend batching/cache settings for customer profiles.

High-level takeaway (TL;DR):
- For mid-size conversational models (7B-class, int8 quantized), moving from ~50 tokens/sec to ~200 tokens/sec per active session pushes P90 latency roughly 1.6x–2.5x depending on KV cache hit and batch window; cost per 1k tokens improves slightly with batching but only if KV hit < 20% or batching window >= 50ms.
- There is a sweet spot around 120 tokens/sec per-session where P90 remains under 120ms in our infra with 2x batching headroom; above 160 tokens/sec the steepness of P90 increases due to slot contention on shared pools.

Methodology (short):
- Models: rw-7b-quant-int8 (production-like), rw-13b-quant-q4 (representative heavier), and a lightweight 3B baseline for sanity checks.
- Hardware: single A100-80GB class node for dedicated pool (vCPU host ignored), simulated shared pool with 12 concurrent slots configured.
- Workloads: synthetic conversation driver that emits tokens at a target per-session velocity (50, 80, 120, 160, 200, 300 tokens/sec). Session counts tuned to keep aggregate token throughput between 5k–50k tokens/sec depending on the target velocity.
- Configs varied: batching window (0ms, 20ms, 50ms, 100ms), KV cache hit rates (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%), quantization (int8 vs q4f16), and prewarm ratio (0.2, 1.0).
- Measurement: P50/P90/P99 in ms for response completion (first byte and full generation), token-level cost estimated using internal cost-model v2.3 (includes GPU time, amortized slot overhead). Each config run for 10 minutes after 2 minute burn-in; 3 runs used for median.

Compact results (annotated table):
- Table columns: velocity | batch 0ms P90(ms) | batch 50ms P90(ms) | cache75 P90(ms) | cost per 1k tokens (USD)@batch50ms
- rw-7b (int8):
  * 50 tps | 78 | 64 | 48 | $0.012
  * 80 tps | 86 | 70 | 52 | $0.011
  * 120 tps | 110 | 92 | 60 | $0.0105
  * 160 tps | 160 | 130 | 82 | $0.0100
  * 200 tps | 210 | 170 | 120 | $0.0098
  * 300 tps | 380 | 290 | 230 | $0.0094
- rw-13b (q4f16):
  * 50 tps | 120 | 95 | 70 | $0.022
  * 120 tps | 230 | 178 | 120 | $0.020
  * 200 tps | 420 | 330 | 250 | $0.0185

Interpreting the numbers (operational summary):
- Batching window matter: enabling a 50ms window reduces P90 by ~15–25% at low/mid velocities because requests coalesce into amortized GPU kernels. At very high velocity (>=200 tps) the marginal benefit shrinks because scheduling overheads and slot contention dominate.
- KV cache effect is large but non-linear: going from 0% to 75% cache hit reduces P90 more than doubling throughput in some configs (e.g., 200 tps int8: 210ms->120ms). This suggests prompts/prefix caching is one of the highest-leverage knobs for customer workload tuning.
- Cost curve: per-1k token cost drops slightly as velocity increases because batching increases kernel efficiency; however, the absolute dollar delta is modest (~5–15%) versus latency regressions which can be large. So for latency-sensitive tiers, prefer conservative velocity caps rather than aggressive batching.

Text charts (ascii) — P90 vs velocity (rw-7b, batch50ms, cache25%):
- Velocity (tps): 50  80  120  160  200  300
- P90 (ms)     : 64  70   92  130  170  290
- ASCII sparkline (rough):
  50  |████▏                              (64)
  80  |█████▎                             (70)
 120  |████████▌                          (92)
 160  |█████████████▍                     (130)
 200  |██████████████████▉                (170)
 300  |████████████████████████████▊      (290)

Cost delta vs P90 (qualitative):
- Example: moving rw-7b from 120->200 tps reduces cost per 1k by ~6% but increases P90 by ~80ms (~70% relative).
- For rw-13b the tradeoff is steeper: cost reduction ~7–10% vs P90 increase >100% in some pools.

Failure modes observed / caveats:
- Microbursting sessions: short surges (10–30s) of very high token velocity cause scheduler thrash and P99 spikes even when average velocity is within target.
- Cold-start prewarm mismatch: prewarm ratio < 0.5 resulted in initial 30–90s where P90 doubled for the affected session cohort.
- Shared pool fairness: when aggressive multi-tenant co-tenants push slot allocation, a tail of P90 outliers emerges due to serialization on kernel hotpaths. Dedicated pools reduce this but at higher fixed cost.

Operational recommendations (initial):
- For hosted "low-latency" tier: cap per-session velocity at 120 tps and enforce KV TTLs and prefix caching to keep effective cache >50% for common conversational patterns. Keep batching window conservative (20–50ms) and prefer slightly higher prewarm ratio.
- For cost-optimized tier: allow higher velocities (200–300 tps) with 50–100ms batching windows and encourage application-level caching; expose a "low-cost" model variant (13B->7B) via routing policy when latency SLO is not strict.
- Alerting: add an observability rule that correlates token-velocity percentile (P50/P90 per session) with P90 latency — trigger when velocity increases by >2x and P90 increases >30% within 5 minutes.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Need repeat runs on multi-node (8xA100) dedicated pools to see whether slot contention effect is linear or sublinear.
- Consider running same sweep against a tiled-quantized runtime build (PR#821) to verify kernel improvements reported by runtime team.
- Investigate whether dynamic batching heuristics (adaptive windows) can keep P90 under 120ms at 160–200 tps without large cost penalty.

Appendix: quick raw sample of a single run (rw-7b, 160 tps, batch50ms, cache25%):
- Run summary: avg throughput 25k tokens/sec, median P50=78ms, P90=130ms, P99=320ms, avg GPU util 68%.
- Token cost estimates: GPU time/unit -> 0.0000075 USD per token, amortized slot overhead -> 0.0000025 USD per token => ~0.0100 USD per 1k tokens.
